The price ceiling at $10 is a horizontal line where MC is. The firm can't charge more than $10, so up to Q=110 its MR is $10, which equals MC. It produces where P=10 meets demand: 120-Q=10, so Q=110.
answers.final_answer: Regulated price is $10, the horizontal line at MC. Q_R = 110, where demand crosses P=MC.

answers.brief_reasoning: Allocative efficiency needs P=MC. At Q_M=55, P=$65 is above MC=$10. That means consumers value extra units more than they cost to make, but those units are not produced.
answers.final_answer: At Q=55, price ($65) is greater than MC ($10). Output is restricted below the efficient 110 units. Units 55 to 110 are worth more to buyers than they cost to produce, so they would add surplus, and leaving them out creates deadweight loss.

answers.brief_reasoning: At P=10 and Q=110: TR = 1100 and variable cost = 1100. So profit = 1100 - 1100 - 100 = -100.
